scope.definition: Workflow, not a tool catalog: intake of an idea/bug/incident into a structured ticket; an explicit PLANNING/NOT_READY state; clarification and product/technical plan approval; decomposition into bounded issues/tasks; acceptance criteria; assignment to a human or coding agent; issue-to-branch-to-PR traceability; verification, review, merge and closure.
included: Agent execution initiated from issues or approved plans
Acceptance criteria as review and test oracles
Human gates, security controls, and feedback to templates/evals.
excluded: Autonomous deployment/operations except the merge handoff
A generic comparison of coding-agent platforms
Claims that a prose spec is automatically correct or that passing tests proves product fitness.
scope.foundation: Uses Shape Up pitches for problem/appetite/rabbit-holes/no-gos [S15], RFC 2119 normative strength [S22], and executable Given/When/Then examples [S21].

current_state: Verified platform capability: GitHub and GitLab can structure intake, relate child work, store templates in the repository, link changes to tickets, enforce branch checks/reviews, and close tickets on merge [S1][S2][S3][S7][S12].

Verified agent loop: GitHub Copilot cloud agent can research, plan and change one repository/branch and produce one PR; GitLab Software Development Flow gathers repository and issue/MR context, creates a plan and stages changes under user control [S5][S14].

Verified event automation: GitHub Copilot automations can triage new issues and open draft PRs on repository events or schedules; tools are scoped, but personal automations are private and not Git-versioned [S24]. GitHub Agentic Workflows offer repository-versioned natural-language workflows with declared permissions and safe outputs, but remain public preview [S25].

Specification frameworks are usable but outcome evidence is immature. Spec Kit 1.0 encodes constitution→specify→plan→tasks→implement [S8]; Kiro encodes requirements/bug analysis→design→tasks with optional approvals [S10]; OpenSpec offers an alternative artifact-guided, brownfield-oriented process [S11]. These are implementation mechanisms and vendor/project claims, not comparative proof.

The operationally safe pattern is not “issue opened→agent codes.” It is “intake→triage→PLANNING→READY approval→agent executes→independent verification/review→merge.” GitHub itself says assigned issues should be clear and well scoped with complete acceptance criteria [S4], and its review documentation requires the same thorough review as any contribution [S6].

representative_systems.role: Issue forms, sub-issues, project fields/automation, PR linking/closure, protected branches [S1][S2][S3][S7].
representative_systems.status: Core tracker controls mature; issue forms still documented as public preview [S1].

representative_systems.system: GitHub Copilot cloud agent and Automations
representative_systems.status: Productized with important one-repository/one-PR/59-minute constraints [S5]; automation governance has a versioning/visibility weakness [S24].

representative_systems.role: Workflow-as-code for triage/CI investigation/docs and bounded outputs [S25].
representative_systems.status: Emerging public preview, despite useful hardened compilation and least-privilege design.

representative_systems.system: GitLab issues/templates and Software Development Flow
representative_systems.role: Repository templates plus context-aware plan/stage workflow [S12][S14].
representative_systems.status: Flow generally available in GitLab 18.8; risks and local execution remain material [S14].

representative_systems.role: Repository artifacts and commands separating intent, technical plan, tasks and implementation [S8].
representative_systems.status: Active open-source framework; no independent comparative production outcomes found.

representative_systems.role: requirements.md or bugfix.md, design.md, tasks.md; approval or Quick Spec paths; dependency-wave execution [S10].
representative_systems.status: Product feature; vendor claims, no independent outcome study found.

representative_systems.role: Iterative artifact-guided SDD for brownfield and greenfield projects [S11].
representative_systems.status: Active open source; efficacy not independently established.

representative_systems.role: Cursor plugin workflow by poteto with feature, bugfix and multi-phase plan playbooks [S27][S28][S29][S30].
representative_systems.status: Concrete, auditable workflow source; identity is likely but must be confirmed because “PStack” also names unrelated projects and ports. No independent outcomes found.

primary_evidence.claim: Structured forms can require fields, dropdowns and attestations, while sub-issues preserve parent progress and hierarchy.
Issue-to-PR linkage provides in-progress visibility and closes only when a linked PR reaches the default branch.
An ideal coding-agent task has a clear problem, complete acceptance criteria and file guidance.
primary_evidence.classification: vendor operational guidance, plausible and directly applicable

primary_evidence.claim: Spec artifacts can formally separate policy, behavioral intent, architecture, tasks and implementation.
primary_evidence.evidence: Spec Kit, Kiro and OpenSpec source/docs [S8][S10][S11].
primary_evidence.classification: verified artifact/workflow capability, not verified benefit

primary_evidence.claim: Repository controls can stop direct/unsafe merges and require checks/reviews.
Human review remains an explicit boundary for agent output and privileged CI.
primary_evidence.evidence: Copilot review rules and GitLab accept/modify/reject flow [S6][S14].

primary_evidence.claim: pstack treats planning as work, not a preamble: feature work studies and architects before delegation; multi-phase planning produces a validated plan and stops until operator go; bugs reproduce and establish cause before fix implementation.

independent_evidence.finding: SWE-bench formalized issue-text-to-patch evaluation from 2,294 issue-linked PR tasks in 12 Python repositories [S16][S17]. This demonstrates a reproducible loop, not autonomous product ownership.

SWE-Bench+ manually audited successful patches and reported 32.67% solution leakage and 31.08% suspicious successes due to weak tests; filtering reduced SWE-agent+GPT-4 from 12.47% to 3.97% [S18]. This directly warns that acceptance tests can be incomplete and benchmark pass rates can overstate issue resolution.

METR’s randomized trial found experienced maintainers took 19% longer with early-2025 AI [S19]. A 2026 follow-up produced apparent speedups but wide confidence intervals and serious selection/time-measurement bias, so the authors call the evidence weak [S20].

DORA 2024 found AI benefits at the individual level alongside worse delivery throughput and stability; it emphasizes small batches and robust tests [S26]. Association and survey design do not isolate issue-planning quality, but contradict simple “more generated code equals better delivery” claims.

independent_evidence.gap: No independent controlled comparison located that isolates Spec Kit, Kiro Specs, OpenSpec or pstack against ordinary high-quality issue planning in production.

metrics.meaning: Coverage of real issue-linked PR patterns, but limited ecosystem and retrospective construction.
Historical 2023-era benchmark values, not current production reliability.

Stars, downloads and vendor testimonials were not treated as efficacy metrics.

reference_workflow.trigger: Issue form, support report, telemetry alert, roadmap idea, dependency event or human request.
reference_workflow.required_inputs: Reporter, problem/evidence, affected users/surface, observed vs expected behavior, reproduction or use case, urgency, security/privacy flag. Forms reject required omissions [S1].
reference_workflow.output: Immutable intake record plus provenance; no code assignment.

reference_workflow.actions: Deduplicate; classify bug/feature/chore/security; set owner, priority, appetite/budget and affected repositories; link incidents/designs. Reject spam and route security reports privately.
reference_workflow.exit: A named planner accepts ownership; otherwise remain INBOX or close with reason. Shape Up’s problem/appetite/rabbit-holes/no-gos is a useful compact frame [S15].

reference_workflow.actions: Inspect repository/history; reproduce bugs; state root-cause hypothesis confidence; define what/why before how; record constraints, dependencies, data/API/schema changes, rollout/rollback, risks and observability. Use normative MUST/SHOULD/MAY consistently [S22]. For large work, create spec/design/task artifacts [S8][S10].
reference_workflow.hard_rule: Implementation agents may read/prototype in an isolated branch, but may not create the production implementation PR. A prototype must be tagged disposable and its findings linked.

reference_workflow.trigger: Any missing product decision, irreproducible bug, contradictory requirement, undefined acceptance predicate, cross-team dependency, security-sensitive capability, or estimate beyond configured limit.
reference_workflow.actions: Ask one bounded question with evidence and options; assign decision owner and deadline. Empirical questions go to a spike/prototype; product/value/risk decisions go to a human. If unanswered, return to backlog, narrow scope, or close—not guess.

readiness_checklist: Bug has reproducible failing evidence or documented exception
Acceptance criteria are observable, atomic, include negative/error paths, and map to tests/manual evidence
Affected surfaces/repositories and dependencies are known
Implementation approach and alternatives/tradeoffs are recorded
Tasks fit one repository/branch/PR/time budget or are decomposed
Security, migration, rollout, telemetry and rollback requirements are set
Reviewer, test commands/environments, and evidence artifacts are named
reference_workflow.output: Versioned plan/spec and child issues. GitHub sub-issues preserve hierarchy [S2].

reference_workflow.gate: A product owner approves behavior/scope; a technical owner approves design/decomposition; security/data owner approves elevated-risk work. Record approver and spec revision/hash. Two-person approval can be one combined meeting but must cover both decisions. pstack’s multi-phase playbook similarly stops after validated plan delivery until explicit operator go [S29].

reference_workflow.trigger: Only READY items enter agent/human queues. Freeze the accepted spec revision; create branch/worktree; lease task to one owner; agent receives only the bounded issue, repo instructions and tools. Parallelize only child issues with disjoint files/state; serialize migrations/shared invariants. pstack makes this decomposition checkpoint explicit [S28].

reference_workflow.outputs: Small PR links issue/spec revision and child issue, describes scope/no-gos, implementation, risks, generated tests and evidence. Use closing keywords only for the final/default-branch PR [S3].
reference_workflow.checks: Deterministic unit/integration/e2e/static/security checks; acceptance-criterion trace matrix; same-surface bug reproduction; diff-size/change-surface budget; no unexplained generated artifacts.

reference_workflow.gate: Independent reviewer challenges behavior, design, tests and spec conformance. For agent PRs, author/assigner approval cannot satisfy GitHub’s required reviewer count; privileged Actions require explicit approval by default [S6]. Any spec change returns to PLANNING and increments revision.
Required checks and approvals, no unresolved threads, rollout/rollback ready. Protected branch blocks bypass [S7]. Merge to default branch closes linked issue [S3].

reference_workflow.actions: Observe rollout and acceptance signals. Close only when deployed/observed if merge is not completion. Reopen/regress on failed criteria; link the failure to template, instruction or eval updates. Measure lead time by state, clarification rate, rework/reopen rate, escaped defects, reviewer time and cost—not code volume.

integration_points.mechanics: GitHub YAML issue forms [S1] or repository-stored GitLab .gitlab/issue_templates/*.md [S12]; validate required evidence; webhook queues a triage job.
Version specs beside code (for example, constitution/spec/plan/tasks [S8] or requirements/design/tasks [S10]); link exact commit/hash in issue; CODEOWNERS review applies.
Map explicit status field INBOX/TRIAGED/PLANNING/CLARIFICATION_REQUIRED/READY_REVIEW/READY/IN_PROGRESS/VERIFYING/REVIEW_REQUIRED/DONE; never infer readiness from assignment alone.
Parent/sub-issue API and project progress [S2]; each executable issue stores dependencies, repository, predicted time, risk and acceptance subset.
GitHub issue assignment/prompt to Copilot [S4][S5], GitLab issue/MR context to Software Development Flow [S14], or queue/webhook to another agent. Require readiness token/spec hash before dispatch.

Prefer versioned GitHub Agentic Workflows with declared triggers/permissions/safe outputs [S25]. If using Copilot automations, export/configure governance separately because creator-private automations are not Git-versioned [S24].
Ephemeral worktree/container, pinned dependencies, repo instructions, deterministic setup/tests; keep write token scoped. Copilot uses an ephemeral Actions environment [S5].
Link PR to issue and accepted spec revision; status checks, code owners, protected branches, scanners, artifact provenance [S3][S7][S23].
Webhook state transitions and collect failure reason, clarification count, test gaps, human edits, reopen/rollback and spend; curate representative failed issues as private regression evals.

human_gates.why: Bots cannot reliably decide product value, duplicate intent, abuse or disclosure channel. Human owns priority/appetite and sensitive routing.

Confirms ticket is planned before implementation. Product owner approves user behavior and no-gos; technical owner approves feasibility, decomposition, test/evidence plan, migration and rollback. High-risk changes add security/data/operations approval.
Human chooses among value/risk tradeoffs. Agent may settle empirical questions with a time-boxed prototype, but may not silently invent policy, UX, compatibility or data-retention decisions.
Approve secret access, network expansion, workflow-file modifications and CI execution. Copilot-created workflow runs are held for approval by default [S6].
Tests can encode an incomplete oracle; SWE-Bench+ documents weak-test false confidence [S18]. Copilot PRs require normal review and a separate required approver [S6].

Required for auth, payments, destructive data changes, public APIs, compliance, migrations or low-confidence output; low-risk categories may auto-merge only after measured pilot thresholds and rollback readiness.
An emergency path may bypass normal planning only with incident commander, narrow reversible patch, logged rationale, post-merge plan/backfill and time-bound follow-up.

failure_modes.effect: Agent treats ambiguous ticket as prompt, optimizes an unstated requirement and creates review churn.
failure_modes.signal: IN_PROGRESS without readiness token; acceptance criteria added after code.
failure_modes.evidence: GitHub recommends well-scoped tasks and complete criteria [S4].

failure_modes.effect: Long generated spec appears precise but embeds hallucinated assumptions or duplicates code; approvals become rubber stamps.
failure_modes.signal: No questions/tradeoffs/no-gos; criteria cannot be observed.

failure_modes.effect: Children conflict on shared schema/files, duplicate work or leave integration gaps; too-large task hits session/tool limit.
failure_modes.signal: Cross-PR shared writes, cycles, repeated rebases, 59-minute timeout [S5].

failure_modes.effect: Patch passes visible tests but violates intended behavior or hidden edge cases.
failure_modes.signal: Generated test mirrors implementation; no negative or same-surface test.

failure_modes.effect: Leaders assume issue-to-PR score predicts throughput, maintainability or product correctness.
failure_modes.signal: Success measured only by closed tickets/pass rate.
failure_modes.evidence: METR and DORA show real-work tradeoffs and uncertainty [S19][S20][S26].

failure_modes.effect: Issue text causes tool misuse, exfiltration or malicious workflow edit.
failure_modes.signal: External reporter text reaches write/network tools.
failure_modes.evidence: Copilot automations ignore non-writer-triggered events by default [S24]; Actions security guidance [S23].

failure_modes.effect: Local agent reads .env or ignored credentials and sends them to model/API.
failure_modes.evidence: GitLab explicitly documents access to untracked and ignored files [S14].

failure_modes.effect: Personal automation behavior changes outside code review/audit.
failure_modes.signal: No repository config or change history.
failure_modes.evidence: Copilot automations are creator-private and not committed to Git [S24].

failure_modes.effect: Issue closes at merge though rollout or acceptance remains unverified; non-default target fails to close.
failure_modes.signal: Closed != deployed; stacked PR keyword used early.

failure_modes.effect: Cheap generation produces expensive human review, CI and rework.
failure_modes.signal: PR arrival exceeds review capacity; Actions/AI-credit burn rises [S5].

failure_modes.effect: No person owns product decision, spec freshness or generated maintenance debt.
failure_modes.signal: Repeated reopen, abandoned PRs, stale READY items.

failure_modes.effect: A team evaluates a fork or unrelated Unix/network pstack as if it were poteto’s workflow.
failure_modes.evidence: Relevant candidate is the poteto plugin in cursor/plugins [S27], but user intent is not confirmed.

controls_and_mitigations: Model readiness as a server-enforced state transition. Dispatch requires READY plus approved spec hash; changing scope invalidates it and returns the item to PLANNING.

Store Definition of Ready as policy-as-code: required problem/evidence, scope/no-gos, criteria, test plan, dependencies, risk, rollout/rollback, owners and unanswered-questions=0. Keep evidence, not check-box prose.
Use bounded clarification: distinguish empirical questions (agent spike) from product/risk decisions (human); offer options with consequences; escalate after SLA; never let silence select a default.

Decompose by independently verifiable outcome and ownership boundary. Keep shared schema/migration first; serialize shared mutable state; cap task time/diff/files and create an integration issue. GitHub hierarchy supports tracking [S2]; Copilot limits make bounding necessary [S5].

Write acceptance criteria as observable predicates and examples, including negative/error/accessibility/performance/compatibility paths; use Given/When/Then where executable [S21], but retain product review because examples cannot exhaust intent.
Bind issue→spec revision→branch→commits→PR→CI artifacts→deployment; reject a PR whose cited spec is stale; use default-branch closing semantics deliberately [S3].
Use least-privilege ephemeral credentials, read-only by default, allowlisted network, no production secrets, pinned Actions, protected branches and required independent review [S7][S23][S25].

Treat external ticket text as untrusted data; do not dispatch it directly to a write-capable agent. Sanitize/quote, require maintainer triage, and preserve Copilot automation’s default writer-only event rule [S24].

Run independent test generation/review; require same-surface bug reproduction and mutation/property tests for critical invariants. Track reopen and escaped-defect rates because benchmark tests can be weak [S18].
Set concurrency, token/minute/CI budgets, retry ceiling, max PR size and review WIP. Quarantine repeated failures; do not automatically broaden scope or permissions.
Canary by risk class. Start docs/tests/small bug fixes; require human merge; auto-merge only reversible, low-risk classes after local data shows acceptable false-positive/reopen/rollback rates.
Version automation in repository where possible. GitHub Agentic Workflows do this [S25]; if using private Copilot automations, maintain an approved exported registry and periodic drift audit [S24].
Audit every state transition, prompt/spec revision, tool call, approval, test artifact, cost and rollback. GitLab reports an audit event per Software Development Flow API request [S14].

maturity_assessment.overall: Conditionally useful and production-ready only as a gated workflow; autonomous backlog-to-merge without human product/technical gates remains emerging/high risk.
mature: Structured intake/templates, issue hierarchy, PR linkage, branch protections and deterministic CI [S1][S2][S3][S7][S12].
Explicit PLANNING/READY state, Definition of Ready and approval are standard workflow engineering patterns, although enforcement is custom.
conditionally_useful: Issue-to-PR coding agents for bounded single-repository tasks with strong criteria and review [S4][S5][S6][S14].
Spec Kit/Kiro/OpenSpec/pstack as scaffolds when artifacts stay reviewable and proportionate [S8][S10][S11][S27][S28][S29][S30].
emerging: Event-driven agent automations and workflow-as-code; powerful controls exist, but some are preview or private/non-versioned [S24][S25].
Parallel multi-agent plan execution; conflict, cost and verification overhead are not well quantified.
not_demonstrated: Reliable autonomous product judgment, specification correctness, cross-repository architectural work, or safe unattended merge/deploy. Independent productivity evidence is mixed and methodologically unstable [S18][S19][S20][S26].

buy_or_adopt: Use GitHub/GitLab native forms/templates/projects/sub-issues/PR protections rather than rebuild tracker primitives [S1][S2][S7][S12].
Use hosted agent flow when repository hosting, policy and data boundary fit: GitHub Copilot [S5][S24] or GitLab Software Development Flow [S14].
Adopt Spec Kit 1.0, Kiro Specs, OpenSpec or pstack selectively for artifact/playbook scaffolding [S8][S10][S11][S27][S28][S29][S30].
custom_engineering_required: Definition-of-Ready evaluator and enforced state machine
build_vs_buy.selection_rule: Prefer repository-native, diffable artifacts and open APIs. Avoid a product whose automation configuration, prompts or decisions cannot be reviewed/exported. Buy execution capacity; build the project-specific control plane and readiness policy.

recommended_pattern.planning_loop: INBOX→TRIAGED→PLANNING↔CLARIFICATION_REQUIRED→READY_REVIEW→READY. It is owned by humans for value/risk and assisted by agents for repository research, reproduction, alternatives and decomposition. No production implementation starts before READY.
recommended_pattern.delivery_loop: READY→leased bounded task→isolated branch/worktree→draft/change set→deterministic verification→independent review→protected merge→deployment observation→CLOSED/REOPENED.
minimum_artifacts: Versioned behavior spec with observable acceptance criteria
Child issues each with one verifiable outcome
PR acceptance trace matrix and evidence links
recommended_pattern.rollout: Pilot 4–6 weeks on low-risk docs/tests and reproducible bugs. Keep human READY and merge gates. Compare against matched baseline: planning time, cycle time, human review minutes, first-pass acceptance, reopen/rollback/escaped defect, CI/AI cost. Expand only when total delivery outcome improves, not when code/PR count rises.
recommended_pattern.pstack_use: If the intended PStack is poteto’s Cursor plugin, borrow three enforceable mechanics: architecture before feature delegation [S28], reproduction/causal evidence before a bug fix [S30], and a validated plan deliverable followed by an explicit operator go before multi-phase implementation [S29]. Do not adopt its model defaults, high parallelism or “overnight” rhetoric without local security/cost/effectiveness tests.
recommended_pattern.bottom_line: The key reusable unit is an approved, versioned, testable plan—not an issue label and not an agent prompt. Agents can accelerate evidence gathering and execution; humans retain intent, risk and merge accountability.

open_questions: Which acceptance-criterion forms best predict first-pass correctness by task class and codebase?
What Definition-of-Ready false-reject rate is tolerable, and who can grant documented exceptions?
How should readiness quality be scored without incentivizing verbose specification theater?
What local thresholds for reopen, rollback, escaped defect, reviewer time and cost justify low-risk auto-merge?
How should a spec revision invalidate or migrate in-flight child issues and agent sessions?
How can cross-repository changes preserve atomic intent and rollback when common agents handle one repository/PR [S5]?
Which independent, controlled evidence shows benefit from Spec Kit, Kiro, OpenSpec or pstack versus disciplined templates and reviews alone?
Does the user’s “PStack” refer to poteto’s workflow in cursor/plugins [S27], a port such as phthomas/pstack, or another system?
How will issue content be isolated from secrets/tools and tested for prompt injection?
What is the post-2026-09-13 status of public-preview issue forms and GitHub Agentic Workflows? Unknown by scope.

confidence.overall: Moderate-high for platform mechanics and recommended gated design; moderate for maturity; low for comparative productivity of named SDD frameworks.
high: GitHub/GitLab tracker, linkage, permission, workflow and documented limit behavior [S1][S2][S3][S4][S5][S6][S7][S12][S13][S14][S23][S24][S25].
SWE-bench/SWE-Bench+ and METR numeric findings as reported [S16][S17][S18][S19][S20].
moderate: Inference that an explicit READY gate plus independent review is the safest reusable production pattern. It triangulates vendor guidance, security controls and benchmark critiques but is not itself tested as one package.
DORA association as directional evidence, not causal proof specific to this workflow [S26].
low: Productivity/quality advantage of Spec Kit, Kiro, OpenSpec and pstack; no independent head-to-head production evaluation located.
PStack identity until the requester confirms; poteto’s cursor/plugins pstack is the strongest relevant match [S27].

conflicts.conflict: Vendor capability framing says coding agents work independently and automate routine development [S5][S24], while GitHub also requires well-scoped tickets and thorough independent review [S4][S6].
conflicts.resolution: Independence describes execution, not correctness or product authority. Keep readiness/review gates.

conflicts.conflict: SWE-bench shows increasing issue-resolution capability [S16][S17], but SWE-Bench+ reports leakage and weak-test inflation [S18].
conflicts.resolution: Use benchmark results only as capability evidence; require local acceptance oracles and review.

conflicts.conflict: METR early-2025 found a slowdown [S19]; late-2025 data suggested speedup [S20].
conflicts.resolution: Tool capability changed, but the follow-up has wide intervals and selection/time-measurement bias. Treat direction and magnitude as unsettled.

conflicts.conflict: Kiro Quick Spec can remove approval gates [S10], whereas the recommended process makes READY approval mandatory.
conflicts.resolution: Use Quick Spec only to draft artifacts; do not let its product shortcut bypass project readiness policy.

conflicts.conflict: Spec frameworks encourage detailed artifacts [S8][S10], while small work can be harmed by ceremony; pstack itself says obvious one/two-file changes may skip a multi-phase plan [S29].
conflicts.resolution: Scale artifact depth to risk, but never skip the minimal READY evidence and approval. “Small” changes use a short plan, not no plan.

conflicts.conflict: Copilot automations offer direct event response [S24], but external issue content is untrusted.
conflicts.resolution: Keep the default writer-only trigger behavior; external intake first enters triage with no write-capable tools.

uncertain.reason: It is the strongest match to software-development workflow/planning and exposes feature, bugfix and multi-phase plan playbooks, but the name also refers to unrelated Unix stack tools, network stacks and multiple ports.
uncertain.needed: Requester confirmation of repository/author; until then cite the exact candidate URL [S27].

uncertain.reason: First-party docs establish mechanics, not comparative outcomes.
uncertain.needed: Independent controlled or longitudinal production study with defects, reviewer time and total cost.
